Bread rises then collapses in the oven

Page 1 of 2 1 2 Next
wren
Member
Posts: 41
12 Feb, 21:04
My sandwich loaf doubles nicely in the tin, but as soon as it goes in the oven the top sinks and I get a dense band under the crust. I use strong white flour, 65 percent water and a packet of instant yeast. What am I doing wrong?
Quote Report
oskar
Moderator
Posts: 3,120
12 Feb, 21:30
That sounds like over-proofing. When the dough has risen too far the gluten is stretched to its limit and the oven spring has nowhere to go, so it falls. Try baking when it has risen by about three quarters, and press it gently: if the dent springs back slowly, it is ready.
Quote Report
hanne
Member
Posts: 7
13 Feb, 08:12
Also check how warm your kitchen is. In summer my dough is ready in forty minutes, in winter it can take two hours, so the time on the recipe is only a guide. A packet of yeast is a lot for one loaf, half of it gives a slower and steadier rise.
Quote Report
wren
Member
Posts: 42
14 Feb, 19:45
Thank you both. I used half the yeast and baked it earlier, at three quarters risen, and it held its shape with a proper dome. Marking this as solved.
